basis: Decision 0018 and docs/wire/export.md. Encoded bytes are hand-derived from ontos-codec-v1 (Atom=00 length bytes, Tuple=01 arity items) with the 13-octet reference header bitwire/ref/1 and the 19-octet addressed header, then checked against the released 0.5.0 encoder. The export root [x] is an example of a root a composition declares; it is not reserved. Scopes are 16-byte atoms and ids are ASCII decimal. Atoms are hex. The table and lifetime expectations precede any implementation.

table.comment: Paths are relative to the side's export root. A send delivers its message to the export's target once; a release removes the export; refusals are observed by the exporting side's host only.

deliveries.name: a live id under a foreign scope is not an alias
a route with an extra segment

observations: Each delivered send invokes the export's target once with the sent message unchanged; a send through an import is local admission on its connection only.
An export's id is never reused within its scope: after id 1 is released, the next export in that scope has a new id, and a reference with id 1 is refused unknown-reference.
Two connections whose tables both issue id 1: a reference from one, copied onto the other, is refused foreign-reference there, even while that side's own id 1 is live.
A new connection at the same place is a new scope: references issued in the old scope are refused foreign-reference and never reach an export of the new one.
Release removes only the forwarding association. It never closes, releases or refuses the target Wire, and the target stays usable by its other holders.

When a connection ends, every export in its scope ends, and every re-export whose source import came from that connection retires: later sends to them are refused unknown-reference on the side that issued them.

Fan-out: one import re-exported on two connections stays imported while either re-export is live. Releasing one re-export sends no upstream release, and a send through the surviving branch still reaches the original target. Releasing the last dependent sends exactly one upstream release.
A host may hold an import locally as a dependent of its own; the upstream release waits for that holder too.

A reply crossing two forwarding boundaries: the caller exports its Wire, each forwarding side re-exports the import it received, and a send through the final import reaches the caller's Wire once. A refusal at any side is observed there and sends nothing toward anyone.
Exporting beyond a table's bound fails locally with export-limit and does not affect existing exports.
The connection's dispatcher remains its single receive owner; exports add routes to it, and import grants sending only.
